artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of the first tome of
Migne's Liturgia Mozarabica, Patrologia Latina 85, the Missale mixtum, 114,783
LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR bytes, no form feeds, no NUL bytes,
ending in a newline. At 4.6 MB it is the largest file this lane acquired.
Registered as a source artifact and nothing more; deliberately NOT structured as
liturgical records. THERE ARE NO PAGE BOUNDARIES IN THIS FILE except the Google
front matter's.

WHICH TOME THIS IS, WHICH IS THE FINDING THAT KEPT AN OFFICE BOOK OUT OF A
MISSAL'S IDENTITY. This is PL LXXXV, `TOMUS PRIOR`, read at line 192 as
`PATROLOGIJB LATINM TOMUS LXXXT.` and at line 346 as `TOMUS PRIOR`, with the
running signature `PATROL. LXXXV.` down the volume. The commissioning brief named
`liturgiamozarab00churgoog` as a duplicate of this item. IT IS PL LXXXVI, `TOMUS
POSTERIOR`, the Breviarium Gothicum -- Lorenzana's BREVIARY, 819 leaves, a
different book by a different editor carrying the office and not the Mass. It is
not registered anywhere in this repository and is named here so that the next
reader does not have to re-derive that. The two items share the set title
`Liturgia Mozarabica ... in duos tomos divisa`, which is the whole reason the
confusion is easy, and the Internet Archive's own `volume` fields (1 and 2) are
the quickest way to tell them apart.

OCR QUALITY, AND IT IS THE BEST IN THIS ACQUISITION. Measured here by
scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a Latin function-word share of 0.1301 over 578,283
tokens, English 0.0267, classified `prose-latin`. The damage that remains is the
ordinary Migne damage and is documented elsewhere in this repository as worse
than it looks: guidance/catena.md measures PL 34's text layer at roughly one
corrupted word in eight. The characteristic failure here is the e/c confusion in
a small type at a tight double-column measure (`cxpirc` for expire, `thc` for
the, `Whcthcr` for Whether -- visible in the English of the Google notice, where
a reader can check it against known words, and present throughout the Latin where
a reader cannot). Migne sets two columns to the page and the scan interleaves
them, so consecutive lines frequently belong to different columns. Read a locus,
do not read a run. A raw-line search over this artifact establishes a lead and
not a finding.

WHAT THE FILE CONTAINS AND WHERE, READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Google's `Usage
guidelines` page occupies lines 1 to about 46. The Harvard bookplate is at line
410. Migne's series title page, `PATROLOGIAE CURSUS COMPLETUS`, is at about line
192; `TOMUS PRIOR` at 346; Monaldini's 1755 dedication to Benedict XIV is
reprinted from about line 415. Lesley's preface and notes follow, and the Missal
occupies the body. The footnote on the authorship of the Canon citing Trent is at
leaf n585.

IDENTITY AND EXTENT. Internet Archive item `liturgiamozarab01churgoog`, 685
leaves, `imagecount = 685`, matching the 685 `<OBJECT>` elements of the item's
own djvu.xml counted here. Google id tRCtEGo_VvsC, OCLC 38607172, contributor
Harvard University, scanned 2006-05-25, uploaded 2008-03-05 by `tpb`, `volume =
1`. The companion page-image container is the item's
`liturgiamozarab01churgoog.pdf`, 59,175,281 bytes, which is not registered.

WHAT A READER MUST DO BEFORE READING ANY LITURGY OUT OF THIS BOOK. `read_from =
"not-read"` on the Mozarabic witness rows in
src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml is still correct and was not
touched by the lane that wrote this record. Nothing in this repository has read a
unit of the Mozarabic use. Note also that this edition is a witness at one remove:
what it prints is Lesley's 1755 book, so a reading taken here is a reading of
Migne's reprint of Lesley's reprint of Cisneros, and the 1755 artifacts of the
sibling edition are the nearer witness.
artifacts.rights_basis:
Public domain in the United States because the book was first published outside
the United States before the pre-1931 line, and on that ground alone. The
qualification about Google's own front matter, which is in the bytes and not in
the book, is the same one set out on
artifact.archdiocese-of-toledo.missale-mixtum-mozarabicum.rome-monaldini-1755.missale-mixtum-1755-nypl-text-ed70e3ae
and is repeated in short below.

THE LINE, AND THE YEAR IT WAS DERIVED FOR. Any work first published abroad before
1931 is out of United States copyright; that is the line guidance/missals.md
records from Cornell's public-domain chart as current on 1 January 2026. THE LINE
MOVES EVERY JANUARY -- guidance/missals.md:249 states it in terms -- so it is
written here as DERIVED FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2026 and not as a standing rule: on
1 January 2027 it becomes before 1932, and a later reader must re-derive it
rather than quote this sentence. Publication at Paris in 1862 clears the 2026
line by sixty-nine years and the 2027 line by seventy. URAA restoration cannot
reach it: a restored term runs at most 95 years from publication, which for 1862
ended in 1957. THIS IS THE NARROWEST MARGIN IN THIS ACQUISITION AND IT IS STILL
NOT NARROW; nothing about the annual movement of the line can ever bring 1862
back inside it.

THE DATE WAS TESTED AGAINST THE BOOK'S OWN PAGES. A thirty-two-probe anachronism
battery over all 685 leaves found St Pius X absent, the Queenship absent, St
Joseph the Worker absent, Christ the King absent, St Therese absent, the
Immaculate Heart as `duplex II classis` absent, `Signum magnum` and its
dropped-initial form `ignum magnum` absent, the 1960 class ranks absent, the
restored Holy Week absent, St Joseph in the Canon absent, and John XXIII and the
Second Vatican Council absent. Its one hit was `Tridentinum (sess. 2, cap. i)` in
an editorial footnote on the authorship of the Canon at leaf n585 -- a
nineteenth-century editor citing a sixteenth-century council. THE ONE POST-1862
DATE IN THE FILE IS A LIBRARY STAMP: line 410 reads `HARVARD COLLEGE LIBRARY /
TREAT FUND / CHARTRAND COLLECTION / JUNE 8, 1928`, the accession plate of the
copy that was scanned. It dates Harvard's acquisition of the volume and not
Migne's press, and 1928 is in any case before the line. This test was run because
two acquisitions had already been refused for failing it, the 1920 Missale
Romanum and the Braga digitisation, and because 1862 is late enough in the
nineteenth century that a nineteenth-century book with twentieth-century matter
bound in is a real shape rather than an imaginary one. The probes and their
negatives are listed in
src/sources/inventories/ambrosian-and-mozarabic-rights-v1.toml.

THE SCAN AND ITS TEXT LAYER ADD NOTHING FOR ANYONE TO OWN. A faithful mechanical
reproduction of a public-domain work is not original authorship (Bridgeman Art
Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)), and machine optical
character recognition adds no human authorship on top of it: this text layer was
produced autonomously by ABBYY FineReader 8.0, per the item's own `ocr` field,
converted by `abbyy-to-hocr 1.1.11`, and there is no author to hold a right in
it. MIGNE'S OWN EDITORIAL MATTER IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE SCAN'S AND IS
NOT REACHED BY BRIDGEMAN AT ALL: the prefaces, footnotes and apparatus in this
volume are Migne's and Lesley's original authorship, not a reproduction of
anything. They are free for the same reason the liturgy in it is free -- first
published in 1862 and 1755, both before the line -- and not because a scan adds
nothing.

GOOGLE'S OWN FRONT MATTER IS IN THESE BYTES. Lines 1 to about 46 are Google's
`Usage guidelines`, modern prose of Google's authorship scanned in at the front
of the volume, asking that the files be used for personal, non-commercial
purposes and that the attribution not be removed. The position is the one taken
on the sibling 1755 artifact: Google wrote and inserted that page precisely to
travel with the file and asks in it that it not be removed, which is an implied
licence to redistribute it unaltered and is what is done; the non-commercial
sentence is a request and not a condition of a licence to the book; and Google's
own text says `Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their
custodians`, asserting no copyright in the 1862 book or in the scan. The whole of
the rest of this file is the book, and the notice's boundary at line 46 is one
of the few real boundaries any of these files has.

NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the
download succeeded, or that the item is marked `possible-copyright-status =
NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT`. guidance/sources.md:395-400 holds the first two insufficient
for `tracked`, and the third is a host's guess about a book.

edition.authority: None. A commercial publisher's reprint series. Migne holds no authority over the Mozarabic rite and claims none; what he reprints is Lesley's 1755 book.
edition.notes:
WHICH VOLUME THIS IS, AND WHICH ONE THE OTHER ITEM IS. The two-tome set is
Patrologia Latina 85 and 86 and only the first is a missal. This record is
PL LXXXV, `TOMUS PRIOR`, the Missale mixtum -- read at leaf n192 of the text
layer, `PATROLOGIAE LATINAE TOMUS LXXXV`, and at n346, `TOMUS PRIOR`, with the
running signature `PATROL. LXXXV.` down the volume. Internet Archive item
`liturgiamozarab01churgoog`, 685 leaves, is that.

THE COMMISSIONING BRIEF CALLED `liturgiamozarab00churgoog` A DUPLICATE OF IT AND
IT IS NOT ONE. That item is 819 leaves, its Internet Archive `volume` field says
`2`, and its own pages say `TOMUS POSTERIOR` at leaf-text line 312 with the
running signature `PATROL. LXXXVI.` throughout. IT IS PATROLOGIA LATINA 86, THE
BREVIARIUM GOTHICUM -- a BREVIARY, Lorenzana's, not a missal at all. It carries
the office and not the Mass, it is a different book by a different editor, and
folding it in as a second copy of the missal would have put an office book under
a missal's identity. It is not registered here because this lane's scope is the
missals of the Latin rites; it is named so that the next lane knows it exists,
knows what it is, and does not have to re-derive that from a shared title page.
The two share the set title `Liturgia Mozarabica ... in duos tomos divisa` and
that title is the whole reason the confusion is easy.

THE DATE TEST. A thirty-two-probe anachronism battery over all 685 leaves found
nothing later than the imprint. Its only hit was `Tridentinum (sess. 2, cap. i)`
in an editorial footnote on the authorship of the Canon at leaf n585 -- a
nineteenth-century editor citing a sixteenth-century council, which is what a
Patrologia footnote does. THE ONE POST-IMPRINT DATE IN THE FILE IS A LIBRARY
STAMP AND NOT A PRINTING: line 410 reads `HARVARD COLLEGE LIBRARY / TREAT FUND /
CHARTRAND COLLECTION / JUNE 8, 1928`, the accession plate of the copy that was
scanned. It dates Harvard's acquisition, not Migne's press, and it is in any case
before the pre-1931 line. Recorded because a sweep that reported `1928 found` and
stopped there would have looked like the Braga finding and is nothing of the
kind.

WHAT THIS EDITION IS A WITNESS TO, AND THE EDGE IT CARRIES. Its own title states
what it reprints -- the first tome contains the Missale mixtum adorned with the
preface, notes and appendices of Alexander Lesley. That statement is the ground
of the `book-states-it` edge the act history draws from the 1755 station, and it
was read here in the book. So this edition is a witness to the 1755 edition at
one remove and to the Cisneros text at two, and it is NOT an independent
recension of the rite.
edition.publication: Liturgia Mozarabica secundum regulam beati Isidori, in duos tomos divisa, quorum prior continet: Missale mixtum praefatione, notis et appendicibus ab Alexandro Lesleo ornatum; posterior: Breviarium Gothicum opera Fr. Ant. Lorenzana recognitum. [Paris]: excudebatur et venit apud J.-P. Migne editorem, 1862. PATROLOGIAE LATINAE TOMUS LXXXV, TOMUS PRIOR. The copy digitised is Harvard College Library's, from the bequest of John Harvey Treat, scanned by Google and uploaded to the Internet Archive as item liturgiamozarab01churgoog.

work.author: Archdiocese of Toledo
work.description: The altar book of the Hispano-Mozarabic rite -- the old Spanish rite, the Visigothic and Isidorian use of the peninsula, suppressed for the Roman use in the eleventh century and kept alive at Toledo, where Cardinal Ximenez de Cisneros endowed the chapel of Corpus Christi in the cathedral for its celebration and had the Missale mixtum printed in 1500. IT IS NOT THE MISSALE ROMANUM AND MUST NOT BE FILED WITH IT: its Mass has its own shape, with the Illatio for the Preface, the Post pridie for what the Roman book puts after the institution narrative, the fraction of the Host into nine particles, and the Creed said after the consecration. It is registered under the archdiocese of Toledo because Toledo is the church whose ordinary has held and legislated for the rite continuously -- Cisneros for the 1500 printing, Lorenzana for the 1770s recension that Migne reprints -- on the same pattern as work.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense. NEITHER EDITION REGISTERED HERE IS A TYPICAL EDITION AND NEITHER IS AN ACT. Both are scholarly reprintings of the Cisneros book: Alexander Lesley's of 1755, printed at Rome with his own preface, notes and appendix, and Migne's of 1862, which reprints Lesley in the Patrologia Latina. The rite's own modern book, the Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum promulgated at Toledo in 1991 and 1994, is in copyright, was not acquired, and has no record here.
work.title: Missale mixtum secundum regulam beati Isidori dictum Mozarabes
